original_question: Convene a panel on one subject only: the design of docs/index.html as a designed object (not its correctness, not the governance system behind it) -- a full design critique (hierarchy, typography, spacing, colour, the tag strip, phone/desktop, light/dark), every label and sentence judged as writing, new ideas costed, and tensions named rather than resolved, with particular focus on whether design can do better than a sentence for the preference/toleration/abstention/objection problem.
clarified_scope: Single-panel investigation by design, per the brief's own framing -- not a multi-panel arc. Scoped explicitly away from ../record-votes-panel/ (the governance-system/vote-mechanism investigation on the same repo), whose R1-R5 and T1-T3 are read but not re-litigated. Confirmed on setup that docs/index.html had been redesigned since that panel ran and that its one unanimous finding (CTA routing) is already fixed in the current file.
environment_note: No browser/screenshot tool (e.g. Playwright MCP) was available in this session. All layout and 'what the eye lands on' claims are reasoned from the generated markup and CSS cascade, not from a rendered viewport -- flagged throughout panels/panel-01-design.md and research/research-log.md. Contrast ratios were computed directly (WCAG relative-luminance formula), not estimated. findings.md was not written as a separate file in this run -- the harness's report-file restriction applies to it; its content is folded into synthesis.md and was delivered directly to the user in the final turn.
next_suggested: [A] Implementation pass -- ship R6, R9, R10 together (one small copy-and-reclassification commit, no open design questions) and R7 (since-you-were-last-here banner) separately, per the recommendations file's own priority order

[B] A focused follow-up design pass specifically on T2 -- whether a dual-grouping visual treatment for Tier C is worth prototyping and actually rendering (this panel deliberately declined to improvise one under time pressure)
[S] Stop here -- the brief asked for one panel's worth of critique, text, ideas and tensions, and that is what this produced; further panels are optional, not required to close out the brief
